title: How to Grill Sliced Pears and Brie for an Autumn Appetizer
keyword: grilling pears and brie on bbq mat
meta_description: Master the art of grilling pears and brie on a BBQ mat for a perfect autumn appetizer. Keep your grill clean and flavors intact with this easy recipe.
html:
There is nothing quite like the smoky sweetness of roasted fruit to signal the arrival of cool weather. While many people retreat indoors to their ovens come September, the grill actually offers a unique depth of flavor that you just can't get from baking. However, combining delicate fruit with melting cheese on open grates is a recipe for disaster—literally. If you want to avoid losing your brie through the slats or having pears stick to the metal, try grilling pears and brie on bbq mat. This simple tool transforms a potentially messy cleanup into an elegant, fuss-free appetizer that will disappear off the plate in minutes.

The Secret to Grilling Delicate Foods

The biggest challenge with this appetizer is the texture contrast. You need high heat to caramelize the natural sugars in the pears, but that same heat turns brie into a liquid mess almost instantly. Without a barrier, the cheese melts, drips onto the burners, and causes flare-ups, while the pears can soften too much and break apart when you try to flip them.

This is where BBQ Grill Mats become essential. These thin, reusable non-stick mats sit directly on top of your grill grates, creating a flat, solid surface. They allow heat to transfer perfectly for those gorgeous grill marks without the risk of sticking. Because they are non-stick, you can place Brie wedges directly onto the mat without worrying about them fusing to the metal. When you are done, you simply lift the mat off, and your grill stays clean underneath.

Selecting the Right Ingredients

Not all pears are created equal, especially when heat is involved. You want a pear that is firm enough to hold its shape during the cooking process but ripe enough to offer sweetness. Bosc and Anjou pears are excellent choices because they remain firm even when ripe. Avoid Bartlett pears for this recipe; they tend to turn into mush once they hit the heat.

For the cheese, a standard wheel of double or triple-crème Brie works best. You do not need to buy the most expensive import, but do buy a wedge that feels soft to the touch. If the cheese is too cold and hard, it will take too long to melt, potentially burning the pears before the cheese is ready. Take the cheese out of the fridge about twenty minutes before you plan to grill.

Grilling Pears and Brie on BBQ Mat: Step-by-Step

Preparation is key here. You want everything sliced and ready before the grill gets hot, so you aren't rushing. Here is how to put it all together:

  1. Prep the Pears: Slice the pears in half lengthwise and use a spoon or melon baller to remove the core. Slice each half into thick wedges—about four to five slices per pear depending on size. Toss them gently in a bowl with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice to prevent browning.
  2. Preheat the Grill: Get your grill to a medium-high heat, around 375°F to 400°F. Once the grates are hot, place your BBQ Grill Mats down on the grates. Give them a minute to come up to temperature.
  3. Oil the Surface: Even though the mats are non-stick, a light brush of olive oil helps the caramelization process. Brush the pears lightly with oil and place them cut-side down onto the mat.
  4. The Flip: Grill the pears for about 3 to 4 minutes until they have nice golden-brown grill marks. Flip them carefully.
  5. Add the Cheese: Place a slice or wedge of Brie directly on top of each grilled pear wedge. Close the lid for another 2 to 3 minutes. You want the pear to be tender and the cheese to be soft and gooey, not completely melted off.
  6. Finish and Serve: Remove carefully using a spatula. The mats ensure nothing sticks, so sliding the food off is effortless.

Serving Suggestions for Maximum Flavor

While grilled pears and brie are delicious on their own, a few garnishes can elevate this dish from a simple snack to a gourmet starter. The smokiness of the pear pairs beautifully with crunch and acidity.

Consider topping the warm cheese with a sprinkle of chopped walnuts or pecans for texture. A drizzle of high-quality balsamic glaze adds a tartness that cuts through the richness of the Brie. Fresh herbs like thyme or rosemary also add a lovely aromatic note that bridges the gap between the savory cheese and sweet fruit. Serve these alongside a crusty baguette or crostini to soak up any melted cheese, and pair with a crisp Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir.

Cleaning Up Made Simple

One of the best parts of using BBQ Grill Mats is the aftermath. Usually, grilling cheese means spending twenty minutes with a wire brush scrubbing hardened dairy off your grates. With these mats, you let the grill cool slightly, peel the mats off, and wash them in the sink with warm soapy water. They are completely reusable, so you can enjoy this appetizer all autumn long without the headache of cleanup.

FAQ

Do I need to peel the pears before grilling?

No, you do not need to peel the pears. The skin helps hold the fruit together while it cooks and adds a nice texture contrast. Just make sure to wash them thoroughly before slicing.

Can I use a grill pan on the stove instead?

Yes, you can. If you are cooking indoors, a cast-iron grill pan or skillet works well. However, you won't get the same infusion of smoky flavor that you get from an outdoor grill, and you may need a little more oil to prevent sticking.

Is the rind on the Brie edible?

Absolutely. The rind on Brie is safe to eat and adds an earthy flavor that complements the creamy paste inside. It also helps the cheese maintain its shape slightly as it heats up, preventing it from melting away too quickly.
